presentation.title: Openness Matters: Source and Interfaces in the Age of Agents
presentation.toc: Openness has seen a resurgence: open source, open interfaces, and increasingly open models. AI is a big part of why that happens. Agents can read what is open, and reading was always the expensive part. That changes what openness is worth, and it widens where it applies. Coding agents work with implementations, and that's where open source makes the difference. Business agents work with capabilities, and that's where open interfaces matter. Business agents get pointed at everything your business depends on: your own APIs, and the ones of your partners and providers. That gives a familiar idea more weight. API governance works best when it covers the whole landscape your business depends on, both the APIs you publish and the ones you consume. For your own APIs, open source and open interfaces reinforce each other. For everything else, interfaces are what you have to work with. This talk looks at different kinds of openness, where they apply, and what agents need in order to use what you've opened. The place to start is the AI-readiness of the APIs your business depends on, including the ones you didn't build.

slide.title: AI Success Is Not About AI

slide.title: AI Integration Is the New Moat

ul.li: The openness of what you use is a preference and not something you control
The openness of how you consume is architecture and fully yours
The first is one input among many
The second one is a strategy matter
Openness matters to your consumers the same way it matters to you

slide.title: Not Every Task Needs the Frontier

ul.li: Open models now lag the frontier by about four months
Most (business) agent tasks never needed a frontier model
Running models locally changes cost and data exposure
Mixing and tweaking models becomes a real option
A portfolio of models replaces picking one winner
A gateway is the interface to the model layer
Models can be switched without touching applications
Controls, limits, and monitoring end up in one place
As little AI as possible and as much AI as necessary
AI is an implementation detail of a capability
Stable interfaces keep the capability separate from its implementation

slide.title: A Thin Layer, Not a Fat One

ul.li: Skip the API work → jump to MCP → call it AI-readiness
MCP should be a thin layer, not a fat one
Good APIs publish as MCP tools with little effort
The rest need orchestration into tools worth calling
Case in point: Meta Muse supports OpenAPI-based connectors
Internal teams build faster, or believe they have to
Everyone outside builds more and expects you to keep up
Most of that acceleration is outside your control
Optionality is what decides how quickly you can respond
Make AI consumption part of your API governance
Make SLMs and local models part of your strategy
